Elastic Integration SOP

Operating guide for people implementing and maintaining Elastic. Updated for bundled app 18.0.1.7.0, incorporating the distributable connector's 18.0.1.3.1 functionality.

End-to-end workflow

  1. Configure and test separate Beta and Production SFTP connections.
  2. Prepare product identifiers, catalog membership, customers, warehouses, prices and sales representatives.
  3. Optionally import descriptions and governed features from Shopify or another ecommerce source.
  4. Validate one SKU using Inventory Explanation, then generate the required outbound feeds.
  5. Import Elastic orders, inspect staged outcomes and follow the linked Odoo sales order.
  6. Configure independent schedules and monitor logs and source import results.

Guide pages

  • 01 — Connection Setup
  • 02 — Core Configuration and Data Prep
  • 03 — Product Metadata and Feature Import
  • 04 — End File Generation and Manual Exports
  • 05 — Order Import and Staged Orders
  • 06 — Scheduling Imports and Exports
  • 07 — Monitoring and Troubleshooting
  • 08 — Explain Inventory for a SKU

Roles and scope

Elastic users can inspect operational records and generate their own inventory explanations, subject to their Odoo access. Elastic managers maintain configuration, source credentials and mappings. Scheduler users need access to the companies and business records their jobs process.

Shopify, WooCommerce, Magento 2, Shopware 6, PrestaShop, BigCommerce and Odoo product data supply product content. These are feature import sources; they do not replace the Elastic SFTP inventory, customer or order workflows. This bundled app includes all seven sources. The separate p2_elastic_integration distribution installs ecommerce platforms as companion modules; do not install both core applications in one database.

Implementation demo

Use an existing connected client in its approved demo or Beta environment. Show settings and connection health, Shopify field discovery and mappings, one SKU's calculation with sales-order and receipt drill-downs, manual export logs, staged order handling, and schedules. Review customer-specific data before presenting it externally.

01 - Connection Setup

Goal

Create and validate separate SFTP connection profiles for Elastic Beta and Elastic Production, then choose which environment the app should use for all imports and exports.

Prerequisites

  • Elastic SFTP host, port, username, and either password or SSH private key.
  • Elastic outbound, inbound, and archive directory paths.
  • Odoo access in the Elastic Manager group for credential and host-key fields.

Create a Beta Connection

  1. Go to Elastic > Configuration > SFTP Connections.
  2. Create a new connection named Elastic Beta.
  3. Set Environment to Beta / Sandbox.
  4. Enter SFTP host, port, and username.
  5. Select the authentication method: password or SSH key.
  6. Enter Export Directory, Import Directory, and Archive Directory.
  7. Use Fetch & Save Host Key when using verified host keys.
  8. Click Test Connection.

Create a Production Connection

  1. Create another connection named Elastic Production.
  2. Set Environment to Production.
  3. Enter the production credentials and directory paths.
  4. Fetch and save the host key, then test the connection.

Host-Key Policy

Use Verify Stored Host Key for normal operations. This pins the SFTP server key and protects the connection from server impersonation.

Trust on First Connect should only be temporary for troubleshooting. If any connection is still using that policy, the Settings page shows an advisory and the Upgrade Host Keys button.

Link Connections to the Active Configuration

  1. Go to Elastic > Configuration > Settings.
  2. Open the active Elastic Configuration.
  3. On SFTP Connections, select the Beta connection and Production connection.
  4. Choose Active Environment. Use Beta for testing and Production for live data.
  5. Click Test Active Connection.

Operational Rule

All manual exports, scheduled exports, manual imports, and scheduled imports use the active environment's connection. Switch the active environment deliberately and confirm the connection status before running live exports or imports.

02 - Core Configuration and Data Prep

Goal

Configure the data rules that determine which Odoo records are sent to Elastic and how Elastic order files are matched back to Odoo.

File Format Settings

  1. Go to Elastic > Configuration > Settings.
  2. Open Export Settings.
  3. Set Export File Delimiter to comma, pipe, or tab based on Elastic requirements.
  4. Set Export File Encoding. Use UTF-8 unless Elastic requests another encoding.
  5. Keep Include Header Row enabled unless Elastic explicitly requests headerless files.
  6. Set date and datetime formats used by configuration-driven fields.

Enable Export Types

On Export Settings, enable only the files that should be included when using Export All Enabled or the scheduled export job.

  • Products
  • Product Tags
  • Catalogs
  • Catalog Mappings
  • Features
  • Customers
  • Locations
  • Sales Reps
  • Rep Mappings
  • Inventory
  • Prices

Export Filters

Product publication is always gated: a variant must belong to an active catalog through either its template or its own membership, both template and variant must have Push to Elastic enabled, and the product must be an active sellable good with an ItemNumber and StockItemKey. These shared rules govern products, prices, features, tags, inventory and catalog mappings. Inventory additionally requires inventory tracking.

Use Include Quotations in ATP Demand when draft/sent sales quotations should reduce exported inventory availability. Leave it disabled when only confirmed sales demand should reduce ATP.

Enable Send Inventory to Elastic on every warehouse that should contribute inventory. Use Use BOM Component Fallback for ATP when made-to-order finished goods should be sellable based on raw-material stock, and select the BOM Component Categories that should constrain buildable inventory. Components in unselected categories, such as packaging, are ignored. Finished-goods ATP is used first; BOM component availability is only used when the finished good has no positive ATP.

Customer Push to Elastic is always authoritative for customer, location, custom-field and rep-mapping exports.

Customer Setup

  1. Open the customer in Contacts.
  2. On the Elastic tab, confirm Push to Elastic.
  3. Enter Elastic Legacy Account # when Elastic SoldToID should use the legacy account number.
  4. Assign Customer Catalogs when catalog permission should be customer-specific.
  5. Assign Sales Rep from the employee sales-rep records when rep mapping is required. The employee must have a Sales Rep Code.
  6. Assign the customer's Pricelist. The customer export derives its PriceGroup from that pricelist's Elastic Price Group Code.
  7. Set Drop Ship Approved when the custom fields export should send drop_ship = Y.

SoldToID Rule

If Use Legacy Account Number for SoldToID is enabled in Settings, the customer export and order matching use the customer's Elastic Legacy Account # when present. If it is blank, Odoo falls back to the Odoo contact ID.

Product and Variant Setup

  1. Open the product template.
  2. On the Elastic tab, confirm Push to Elastic.
  3. Enter Elastic ItemNumber for the style-level ItemNumber.
  4. Set template-level Product Permission Group, Available Date, and Catalogs when needed.
  5. Open each variant that needs overrides.
  6. Set variant-level Push to Elastic, Elastic SKU, Elastic ItemNumber Override, Elastic Stock Item Key, Product Permission Group, and Available Date as needed.

Catalog Setup

  1. Go to Elastic > Configuration > Catalogs.
  2. Create catalogs with unique codes.
  3. Add product templates, product variants, and customers as needed.
  4. Choose whether catalog mapping lines are generated by Odoo or loaded from an uploaded file.
  5. For generated mapping, set the sort method and click Generate Mapping Lines.
  6. For uploaded mapping, upload the CSV and click Load Mapping Upload.

Pricing Setup

Assign the appropriate Odoo pricelist to each customer. Customer-assigned pricelists are included in prices.csv automatically, and customers.csv uses the same price group. An explicit Elastic Price Group Code is optional; blank codes receive a stable automatic code. Use Send to Elastic only for additional price levels that are not assigned to an exported customer. The product list-price group LP is always included unless an included pricelist already supplies LP.

Customer Cross-References

Use Elastic > Configuration > Customer Cross-References to maintain external Sold-To and Ship-To IDs when order files need explicit mapping to Odoo partners. During order import, mappings are also recorded automatically after a match is found.

03 - Product Metadata and Feature Import

Goal

Prepare Elastic color, size, tag, and feature metadata so product exports and feature exports contain governed values instead of ad hoc text.

Generate Color and Size Metadata

  1. Go to Elastic > Configuration > Settings.
  2. Open the Product Metadata tab.
  3. Click Generate Product Metadata.
  4. Review generated records under Colors, Size Scales, and Size Values.
  5. Clean up codes, color groups, sort orders, alternate sizes, and inactive records before exporting products.

Color metadata is seeded from product attribute values named Color, Colour, Frame Color, or Product Color. Size metadata is seeded from attributes named Size or ending in Size.

Maintain Attribute Value Overrides

Use Elastic > Configuration > Attribute Values or the Product Attribute form to maintain direct Elastic overrides on Odoo attribute values:

  • Elastic Color Code
  • Elastic Color
  • Elastic Color Name
  • Elastic Color Sort
  • Elastic Size Code
  • Elastic Size Name
  • Elastic Size Sort
  • Elastic Alternate Size

Product Tag Mappings

  1. Go to Elastic > Configuration > Product Tag Mappings.
  2. Create one mapping for each TagName Elastic should receive.
  3. Select whether the source field is on product template or product variant.
  4. Select the Odoo field that supplies TagValue.
  5. Choose whether values should be split by line, comma, semicolon, or not split.
  6. Run Export Product Tags or enable Product Tags in Export All.

The product tags export skips color attributes because color is already sent in products.csv.

Governed Feature Setup

  1. Go to Elastic > Configuration > Features.
  2. Create or review the target Elastic features.
  3. Set feature code, display order, type, filterable/searchable flags, and Export to Elastic.
  4. Maintain governed values under Feature Values when controlled values are required.
  5. Use Product Feature Assignments for manual or reviewed assignments.

Ecommerce Feature Sources

  1. In Settings → Ecommerce Features, enable Pull Product Features from an Ecommerce Platform.
  2. Open Configure Feature Sources, or Configuration → Ecommerce Feature Sources. Create a source for each store and language. Choose Shopify for the demo.
  3. For Shopify enter the shop domain, Admin API version and custom-app access token. The GraphQL client defaults to 2026-01. Product reading needs read_products; requesting translations also needs read_translations. Test Connection.
  4. Choose product matching by SKU, barcode, external product ID or handle. Existing imported identifiers are visible in Ecommerce Product Links on the product.
  5. Set the optional language/locale and the Elastic Region. Region defaults to GLOBAL and is exported on feature rows; a locale selects source content and does not itself select an Elastic region.
  6. Run Discover Fields. Review product fields, custom fields/metafields or attributes exposed by that platform. Create mappings to governed Elastic features and choose the appropriate parser.
  7. Shopify supports plain text, multiline text, HTML text, HTML lists, JSON lists and Shopify rich text. A discovered rich-text metafield can be mapped using its suggested parser.
  8. Run Import Features. Inspect the source's last import result, product links and feature assignments before exporting Features to Elastic.

Mappings govern what is imported; discovery does not publish content. Imports match existing Odoo products, upsert assignments and remove stale values within the source and mapping scope. Manual assignments remain separate. Description is a single-value feature per item and region. The shared catalog and identifier gates still determine whether an imported assignment is exported.

Available sources also include WooCommerce, Magento 2, Shopware 6, PrestaShop, BigCommerce and Odoo product data. Each has its own credentials and available fields. Configure sources explicitly; adding support does not connect a store automatically.

Upgrade from legacy Shopify imports

Upgrading carries existing Shopify connections, credentials and mappings into Ecommerce Feature Sources and archives the old connections. Original legacy records remain available for compatibility. With one legacy store, existing product identifiers and imported assignments are linked to the new source. With multiple stores the old schema cannot establish ownership: review product links and old assignments before importing to avoid associating content with the wrong store. Existing business schedules are retained; the new feature-import schedule starts disabled.

Feature Export Rule

The features.csv export reads active Product Feature Assignments where the related feature is active and marked Export to Elastic. Template-level assignments are expanded to active variants. If Export Only Synced Products is enabled, unsynced templates or variants are skipped.
04 - End File Generation and Manual Exports

04 - End File Generation and Manual Exports

Goal

Generate the Elastic outbound files and upload them to the active SFTP connection's export directory.

File Generation Behavior

  • Files are generated with the delimiter, encoding, and header setting from Elastic > Configuration > Settings.
  • File names are stable and do not include timestamps.
  • Each successful export uploads to the active connection's Export Directory.
  • Each export creates an Elastic > Logs > Export Logs record with type, record count, file name, status, and message.

Generated Files

Button / Export File Primary Odoo Source
Export Customers customers.csv Company customers from Contacts
Export Custom Fields customer_custom_fields.csv Customer drop_ship approval and related custom fields
Export Locations locations.csv Customer primary addresses and delivery contacts
Export Products products.csv Sellable active product variants
Export Product Tags product_tags.csv Active product tag mappings applied to product/template fields
Export Features features.csv Active governed assignments, with their source region, for eligible catalog products
Export Prices prices.csv Sellable active product variants and customer-assigned or Elastic-enabled pricelists
Export Inventory inventory.csv Time-phased ATP for storable active products by inventory-enabled warehouse
Export Catalogs catalogs.csv Active Elastic catalogs
Export Mappings catalog_mapping.csv Catalog mapping lines generated by Odoo or loaded from upload
Export Reps reps.csv Active employees marked as Sales Representatives with a Sales Rep Code
Export Rep Mappings rep_mappings.csv Customers mapped through their employee Sales Rep assignment
Export Order Historyorder_headers.csv and order_lines.csvConfirmed and cancelled sales orders, including historical product references

Order history

The history export prepares an 83-column header file and a 56-column line file. It uses confirmed and cancelled orders for eligible company customers in the active company, retaining historical references to archived products. Sections, notes, down payments and shipping lines are excluded; Odoo line IDs provide stable line references. Both payloads are validated before upload. Each file has its own result; SFTP cannot make the two uploads atomic, so investigate a partial failure before rerunning. There is no invoice export feed.

Inventory ATP Logic

The inventory export sends available-to-promise quantities by product and warehouse. It starts with current finished-goods on-hand stock, applies open incoming and outgoing stock moves in date order, optionally subtracts draft/sent quotations, and sends negative quantities as 0. The internal running balance can go negative so later receipts first cover earlier shortages. A backward check then protects future commitments before offering stock at an earlier date. Incoming supply uses the later scheduled date or receipt deadline; demand uses the earlier. The CSV contains cumulative availability, not additive receipt quantities.

If Use BOM Component Fallback for ATP is enabled and a finished product has no positive finished-goods ATP, Odoo evaluates every active BOM for that product/template. Only component lines whose product category is one of the selected BOM Component Categories (or a child category) constrain buildable inventory; unselected categories such as packaging are ignored. For each BOM, the buildable quantity uses the limiting eligible component after reservations and future demand are protected across internal locations in the enabled warehouse. Repeated usage of the same component is combined, and both component and finished output units are converted. Only current physical component stock supports buildable units. If multiple active BOMs exist, Odoo uses the BOM that can build the highest number of finished units. Buildable units supplement physical finished stock without erasing a negative balance. Current and future finished-good demand still reduce availability before export. Shared-component allocation and production lead times are separate policies.

Inventory Examples

  • Future receipts cover old shortages: a SKU has 50 on hand, 75 units of demand due now, 50 units arriving next week, and 100 units arriving the week after. The current row exports 0, next week's row exports 25, and the following receipt increases availability to 125.
  • Negative quantities are never sent: a SKU has 10 on hand and 25 units of future demand before any receipt. The current row already exports 0 because the future demand consumes all current stock. Later receipts first cover the shortage before increasing availability.
  • BOM fallback for MTO goods: a finished good has no finished stock or open manufacturing supply. Frames and lenses are selected as BOM Component Categories while packaging is not. Active BOM A can build 40 units from its frame and lens stock, and active BOM B can build 60; a packaging shortage does not constrain either result. Odoo uses 60 as fallback supply, then subtracts any existing finished-good demand before writing inventory.csv.

Inventory Explanation previews the current calculation for a single SKU and warehouse without generating or uploading a file. It is not a stored historical copy of a previous export. See page 08.

Recommended Manual Export Sequence

  1. Test the active SFTP connection.
  2. Run Generate Product Metadata after product attributes are loaded or changed.
  3. Prepare catalogs and click Generate Mappings if using generated catalog mappings.
  4. Export catalogs.
  5. Export catalog mappings.
  6. Export products.
  7. Export product tags and features.
  8. Export prices.
  9. Export inventory.
  10. Export customers, custom fields, locations, reps, and rep mappings.
  11. Review Export Logs and confirm files appear in the Elastic outbound directory.

Run All Enabled

Use Export All Enabled when all required toggles are configured. This runs each enabled export, summarizes success and failure, and creates individual export logs for each file.

Validation Checklist

  • Products have ItemNumber and StockItemKey values.
  • Customers have SoldToID values that match Elastic expectations.
  • Every customer-assigned pricelist is active; explicit price group codes, when used, are unique.
  • Catalogs have unique codes and mapping lines.
  • Product tag mappings point to fields that still exist.
  • Feature assignments have values and active/exportable features.
  • Export logs show success and expected record counts.

05 - Order Import and Staged Orders

Goal

Poll Elastic order files from SFTP, stage each order/shipment group, and create Odoo draft sale orders with auditability and retry support.

Configure Order Import

  1. Go to Elastic > Configuration > Settings.
  2. Open Import Settings.
  3. Enable Order Import.
  4. Set Order File Pattern, such as *.csv or ORDER_*.csv.
  5. Choose whether to Auto-Confirm Orders. Leave disabled unless the business wants imported orders confirmed automatically.
  6. Choose whether to Archive Processed Files. Keep enabled for normal operation.
  7. Select Stock Item Key Field: UPC / Barcode, SKU, or Product Number + Variation Code + Size.

Manual Import

  1. Confirm the active SFTP environment is correct.
  2. Confirm order files are in the active connection's Import Directory.
  3. Click Import Orders Now.
  4. Review the notification summary.
  5. Open Elastic > Logs > Import Logs.
  6. Open Elastic > Orders > Staged Orders for pending, processed, duplicate, or error rows.

What the Importer Does

  1. Lists matching files in the active SFTP Import Directory.
  2. Downloads each matching file.
  3. Parses the file using the configured delimiter and encoding.
  4. Groups rows by Elastic Order Number and Shipment Number.
  5. Creates or updates one staged order per order/shipment group.
  6. Attempts to create one draft sale order per staged group.
  7. Marks duplicates when a sale order already exists for the same Elastic order and shipment keys.
  8. Writes errors to the staged order record for review.
  9. Moves processed source files to the active connection Archive Directory when archiving is enabled.
  10. Creates an Import Log with file count, order count, error count, status, and summary message.

Staged Order Review

Use Elastic > Orders > Staged Orders to review import outcomes.

  • Pending: staged but not processed yet.
  • Processed: sale order was created.
  • Duplicate: an existing sale order matched the Elastic order/shipment keys.
  • Error: processing failed and the error message needs review.

Retry Procedure

  1. Open the staged order in Error.
  2. Read the error message.
  3. Fix the cause, usually customer mapping, product matching, missing product, or invalid order data.
  4. Click Retry.
  5. If the retry creates a sale order, open it from the staged order.

Matching Notes

  • Sold-To resolution uses connection-aware cross-references, then the supported Odoo ID and legacy account identifiers. Ship-To resolution checks delivery contacts belonging to the Sold-To before accepting a cross-reference; a delivery address from another customer must not be reused.
  • The customer legacy account number can be used as SoldToID when enabled in Settings.
  • Product matching follows the configured Stock Item Key Field.
  • Duplicate checks use the Elastic Order Number and Shipment Number stored on sale orders.

06 - Scheduling Imports and Exports

Open Settings → Configure Schedulers to control six independent business jobs. Each has an enable switch, interval, next execution and Odoo execution user. Intervals support minutes, hours, days, weeks and months.

JobPurpose
Product exportProduct-related feeds selected in Settings
Customer exportCustomer-related feeds selected in Settings
Inventory exportCurrent and dated availability for eligible products and enabled warehouses
Order history exportOrder header and line files
Order importIncoming Elastic files and staged orders
Ecommerce feature importConfigured mappings from each active source

Start with a manual run and inspect its result before enabling a schedule. Enabling an import schedule also enables that import in Settings. Turning its schedule off leaves manual imports available until the corresponding Settings switch is disabled.

Existing schedules survive upgrades. New business schedules start disabled. The source import job processes active sources independently; a failed source is recorded without preventing the others from running. Source result fields show the last attempt and error message.

Choose cadence based on customer needs, data volume and store API limits. Run feature imports before feature exports if the exported content should include the newest source values. Confirm that each selected execution user has the necessary Elastic, Sales, Inventory and company access.

Temporary report cleanup

Elastic: Clean Up Inventory Explanations runs every five minutes. A report becomes unusable after 15 minutes; cleanup removes it and its detail records on the next run. Physical deletion can therefore occur about 15–20 minutes after calculation under normal scheduling, or later if cron is delayed. This maintenance job is active by default and is separate from the six business schedules.

Inspect execution

Settings → Active Schedulers opens active Elastic scheduled actions for administrators. Compare next execution, execution user and job result with Export Logs, Import Logs and each ecommerce source's last-import result. Avoid overlapping duplicate schedules for the same feed.

07 - Monitoring and Troubleshooting

Current diagnostic workflow

For a disputed inventory quantity, use Inventory Explanation for the exact SKU and warehouse. Follow grouped Sales Orders and receipt links, then return using breadcrumbs. Check excluded-product and disabled-warehouse notices before comparing the Elastic preview. The result reflects live Odoo records at calculation time; historical file investigations also require the original exported file and its log.

For ecommerce content, inspect the source's Test Connection, discovered fields, enabled mappings, locale/region, product matching and last import result. Check product links and assignments before rerunning Features export. A successful content import does not mean a file was uploaded.

Daily Monitoring

  1. Open Elastic > Logs > Export Logs and review the most recent export run.
  2. Open Elastic > Logs > Import Logs and review the most recent import run.
  3. Open Elastic > Orders > Staged Orders and filter for Error or Pending records.
  4. Confirm expected files exist in the outbound directory and processed order files moved to archive.
  5. Escalate any failed logs or unprocessed staged orders before the next scheduled run.

Common Export Issues

Symptom Likely Cause Action
No records found Export toggle/filter is too restrictive, records are inactive, or required sync flags are off. Review export filters, active flags, Push to Elastic values, and record eligibility.
No valid records after transformation Required identifiers are missing, such as ItemNumber, StockItemKey, catalog code, or feature value. Review the specific export requirements and fill missing master data.
SFTP upload failed Connection, credential, host-key, or remote directory issue. Test the active connection, verify host key, confirm credentials, and confirm remote paths.
Unexpected price rows Customer-assigned or explicitly enabled pricelists drive price groups; otherwise list price is used. Review customer pricelist assignments and optional Elastic price group codes.

Common Import Issues

Symptom Likely Cause Action
No order files found File pattern does not match, files are in the wrong directory, or the active environment is wrong. Review Order File Pattern, active connection Import Directory, and Active Environment.
No Odoo customer found Missing Sold-To cross-reference or legacy account number mismatch. Create or correct the Customer Cross-Reference or customer Elastic Legacy Account #.
Product not found Order file product key does not match the configured Stock Item Key Field. Review UPC, SKU, or Product Number + Variation Code + Size data in Odoo and the file.
Duplicate staged order A sale order already exists for the Elastic order and shipment keys. Open the linked sale order and confirm no action is needed.
File did not archive Archive path is blank, archiving is disabled, or SFTP move failed. Review Archive Processed Files, Archive Directory, and SFTP permissions.

Recovery Rules

  • Fix master data first, then retry staged orders.
  • Use manual imports and exports to validate fixes before waiting for scheduled jobs.
  • Use Beta for integration testing whenever possible.
  • Keep failed log messages with the incident or support ticket.
  • Do not change the active environment during a scheduled run window.

08 - Explain Inventory for a SKU

Open a spot check

  1. Open Elastic → Inventory Explanation, or open a product's Elastic tab and choose How was inventory calculated?
  2. Select the exact product/SKU and warehouse in your active company. For a template with several variants, select the variant to investigate.
  3. Calculate. Read the calculation time, expiry and any publication notices.

This creates a temporary explanation on demand. It sends nothing to Elastic, needs no SFTP connection and adds no report-writing overhead to normal inventory exports. Reports expire after 15 minutes, are private to their creator, and have no history/list view. Recalculate for a fresh result.

Read the calculation

  • On-hand Inventory: physical internal stock in the chosen warehouse at calculation time.
  • Sales Orders: one grouped line per effective date with the total demand and order count. The link opens the exact orders that contributed; it does not expand every order inline.
  • Incoming Receipts: receipt movements contributing supply. Open the filtered receipts, then their purchase orders through the receipt's source document. Quantities come from outstanding stock movements, not the full original PO quantity.
  • Quotations: draft/sent demand appears only when Include Quotations in ATP Demand is enabled.
  • Other movements: outgoing deliveries, warehouse transfers and moves without a picking remain traceable through their appropriate lists.
  • Running total: balance after that group. Available to Sell: protected daily closing availability after considering later commitments; several groups on one day share the same closing ATS.

Use source and movement links in the current window, then breadcrumbs to return to the calculation. Linked records retain your normal Odoo access restrictions. The lists show current source records; they are not historical snapshots.

Past and future availability

Dates on or before today are folded into today's bucket. Incoming supply uses the later of a movement's scheduled date and deadline; demand uses the earlier. Internal moves wholly within the selected warehouse do not add supply or demand. Cross-warehouse movements affect each warehouse separately.

Starting with on hand, receipts add and demand subtracts to produce dated balances. Deficits carry forward. A backward check reserves today's stock for future demand until replenishment arrives. The exported quantity is the nonnegative minimum balance from that date onward. A current row is always emitted for an eligible SKU/warehouse, even at zero; later rows appear only when the rounded-down quantity changes.

Example: 20 on hand, sales demand of 30 in three days, a receipt of 40 in seven days, and demand of 12 in ten days give running balances 20, −10, 30 and 18. Elastic receives 0 available now and 18 available from day seven. The receipt first covers the carried shortage and the later order.

BOM fallback

Fallback is considered only if finished-goods ATS is zero at every date and the option is enabled. Only configured component categories and their descendants participate. Applicable variant BOM lines are combined by component and converted into product units.

Usable component stock is capped by physical on hand, unreserved stock and demand-protected ATS. Future component receipts cannot be built today. The component table shows required units, available quantities, buildable units and the limiting component. The best buildable quantity from one active BOM is added once; tied BOMs are not summed. Finished-goods deficits and demand still consume that supply. This is a stock estimate, not production capacity or a promised lead time.

What goes to Elastic

The Elastic output preview states Available now or Available from a date and the quantity. The optional raw AvailableDate value uses YYYYMMDD, with blank for today; quantities are rounded down to two decimal places. There is no ambiguous Export row column.

Catalog membership, template and variant Push to Elastic, sellable/storable status, identifiers and the warehouse's Send Inventory to Elastic switch determine publication. An excluded product or warehouse can still be investigated, but has no output preview rows. A disabled Inventory Export setting is called out separately.

The preview uses the same calculation as the exporter at the time you press Calculate. It cannot prove the contents of an earlier file after stock or orders have changed. Compare the original file and export log when investigating a past export.
